mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which reduces corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST by more than 2% over the same month indicates supply chain normalization with reduced housing demand, which boosts corporate efficiency but weakens consumer spending, resulting in mixed but slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% and HOUST < -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls by >2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential increase in RSAFS and PAYEMS over two consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and rising employment, which supports durable goods consumption and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS both rise month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of two consecutive months of rising RSAFS and PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% for three consecutive months signals a risk of deflation, prompting anticipatory monetary easing, which supports equity valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL < 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 3.5% and a fall in PAYEMS below 150000 for the same month indicates labor market imbalances with rising unemployment despite rising participation, which signals economic weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 3.5% and PAYEMS < 150000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 3.5% and PAYEMS < 150000 in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in HOUST above 2% for four consecutive months signals robust housing demand, which correlates with consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months of HOUST > 2% growth.
